timeline.message:
Validate HTTP Method

Motivation:
The HTTP method is a token type defined in [RFC 9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-tokens).
> token          = 1*tchar
> tchar          = "!" / "#" / "$" / "%" / "&" / "'" / "*"
>                 / "+" / "-" / "." / "^" / "_" / "`" / "|" / "~"
>                 / DIGIT / ALPHA
>                 ; any VCHAR, except delimiters

We need to validate the HTTP method to ensure it conforms to the standard.

Modifications:
- Validate the first word of the HTTP request initial line.
- Throw `IllegalArgumentException` if the method is invalid.

Result:
- Fixes [#14201](https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14201#issue-2427986466).

timeline.body:
Motivation:
The HTTP method is a token type defined in [RFC 9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#name-tokens).
> token          = 1*tchar
> tchar           =
>  "!" / "#" / "$" / "%" / "&" / "'" / "*"
>   / "+" / "-" / "." / "^" / "_" / "`" / "|" / "~"
>   / DIGIT / ALPHA
>   ; any VCHAR, except delimiters

We need to validate the HTTP method to ensure it conforms to the standard.

Modifications:
- Validate the first word of the HTTP request initial line.
- Throw `IllegalArgumentException` if the method is invalid.

Result:
- Fixes [#14201](https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14201#issue-2427986466).
I think we could just call `bits.set(...)` directly without the extra loop.

reply.body:
like this?
```
bits.set(0x21, 0x7f);
bits.clear(0x22);//DQUOTE
bits.clear(0x28, 0x2A);//()
bits.clear(0x2C);//,
bits.clear(0x3A, 0x41);//:;<=>?@
bits.clear(0x5B, 0x5E);//[\]
bits.clear(0x7B);//{
bits.clear(0x7D);//}
```

timeline.body:
Another approach could be to move this validation to `HttpMethod` constructor. It already has some validation. If it's not sufficient it could be improved. Advantages:
1. This will help to avoid validation here for the fast path of recognizing `GET/POST` methods as well as `methodMap` lookup inside `HttpMethod.valueOf(...)`.
2. It will cover not only incoming but also outgoing http methods made by netty clients.
3. It will allow you to reuse existing code for token validation from `HttpHeaderValidationUtil.validateToken`.

reply.body: Thank you for the suggestion! It is an appropriate approach. However, regarding point 3, I have a question: Is it allowed to call `HttpHeaderValidationUtil.validateToken` within `HttpMethod`? I understand that `HttpMethod `and `HttpHeader `are not the same concept.
@freeyob I like the suggestion of @idelpivnitskiy ... At worse you could just move the `validateToken(...)` method to `HttpUtil` or so and re-use it from everywhere.
